descriptionChirho: To feel hatred, animosity, or aversion toward a person, thing, or action; the basic Qal active sense covering all finite verb forms (perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive) expressing the emotion or attitude of hatred or strong dislike.

The Qal active participle used substantively to denote a person who hates, i.e. an adversary or enemy; frequently occurs with pronominal suffixes ('those who hate me/you/him/us/them') and functions as a noun meaning 'hater' or 'enemy' in context.

The Qal infinitive construct and absolute forms, used either as a verbal complement ('to hate') or nominally as an abstract noun ('hatred'); includes prepositional phrases (le + infinitive 'in order to hate').
The Qal passive participle describing the state of being hated or unloved; used adjectivally, especially of a disfavored wife ('the hated/unloved one') in legal and proverbial contexts.
The Nifal (passive) stem expressing being hated as a process or event, rather than a state; 'he is hated' or 'will be hated' with dynamic passive force.

labelChirho: Piel ptcp: one who hates intensely
descriptionChirho: The Piel (intensive) stem participle used substantively to denote those who hate with intensity or persistence; functions like the Qal participle but with intensified or iterative force, frequently appearing in lists of enemies or adversaries.
